see.a: Rua João Brícola, 24, Centro. São Bento Metrô station
see.b: The observation deck is on the 34th floor, 160 m above ground. For many decades, it used to be the highest building in town. There is a small museum on the top of the building. Make sure and bring ID (passport) because it is required…
On the rooftop of posh Hotel Unique, Skye serves excellent fusion food under the supervision of chef Emmanuel Bassoleil. Good for night views of the area around Ibirapuera Park.

There are two bars and a couple of posh restaurants with a great view of the River Pinheiros, especially around 18:00, when you can go straight from work or a busy day walking about to watch the sun set above town.

Offer a variety of city tours every weekend. These are mostly walking tours but with some use of the metro. The tour is free of charge, but you will need to take some cash with you to buy metro tickets during the tour as necessary. The…

If you're in São Paulo during the annual Carnival, a national bank holiday between the end of February and March. This is where the typical Carnival parade takes place, with dancers dressed up in costumes and musicians play samba songs…

Every year, during Corpus Christi holidays (usually between May and June), around 3 million people take part in the largest Gay Pride parade in the world. It takes place on a Sunday, and Avenida Paulista is the spot to head to. Floats…

Virada Cultural is a round-the-clock cultural marathon that takes place in various parts of the Historic Center (Downtown), happening yearly around April–May. It is a free event that gathers an audience of several million of people…

The park in front of the Luz station was a meeting point for São Paulo's high society in the early 20th century. It is now a calm and beautiful environment that contrasts with the urban chaos and degradation of its surroundings.
The obelisk in this square dates from 1814, which marks São Paulo becoming a city.
The square holds São Bento's church and monastery, a 17th century monastery, where mass is still held against a backdrop of Gregorian chants. The monks' bakery is a temptation. Give in, it’s no sin.
Church and Convent of Saint Francis and the historic Law School of the University of São Paulo.

The Minhocão ("Big Worm"), a 2.7-km-long highway opened in 1970, is considered to be a monument to poor urban planning and to the chaotic growth of the city in a not-so-distant past. Its construction turned a large portion of the city…

There are buildings that bear witness to many different architectural styles: the 1935 Esther building, considered the first with a modern architectural design; the S-shaped Copan building designed by Oscar Niemeyer; and Itália building…

São Paulo's central square (marked by the Zero Mark (Marco Zero) monument) has fountains, 16 sculptures, palm trees and lots and lots of people. The Sé Cathedral and the São Paulo Justice Palace are located here.
The valley is a giant boulevard with gardens, sculptures and a view of the main downtown office buildings. The Altino Arantes building and the Correios Palace are here.
Linking R. Barão de Itapetininga to R. Direita. Marks the transition from old to the new part of the center.
This exchange is the largest in South America, founded in 1890 by Emílio Rangel Pestana. You can have a visit to the museum inside the building, showcasing Brazil's economic history.

This S-shaped building, the largest residential building of Latin America, was projected by famous Brazilian architect Oscar Niemeyer and was the symbol of the emerging "modern" São Paulo during the 1960s. As the rest of the Historic…

Previously known as the Banespa building (after the bank that used to occupy the building), it was the tallest skyscraper in the city between its completion in 1947 and the construction of the Itália building in 1965. Aside from art…

São Paulo's city hall is a building from the 1930s in modernist architectural style. The building had been the home of Matarazzo Industries, which used to be the most powerful manufacturing company in Brazil.
The first home to the state's mail service, constructed in 1922. It hosts many exhibitions, mainly focused on the company's history.
Home to the Higher Courts of Law of the State of São Paulo since 1933. Hosts an exhibition about law in the state.
Emperor Dom Pedro I's powerful concubine, the Marchess of Santos is one of the most popular monarchy figures in Brazilian popular culture. Her colonial house is now a museum.
A vast baroque basilica decorated with frescoes by Benedito Calixto.

A creepy-looking church in a small street near Liberdade Sq., it is one of the oldest surviving churches of the city, dating back to 1774, when it was built to be the chapel of the city's first cemetery. It is still the destination of…

São Paulo's main catholic church, with 14 towers, built in a Gothic and Renaissance style. Although the current construction was finished in 1954, the original cathedral, at the same spot, dates from the early history of São Paulo - 1616.
Built in the neo-gothic style in 1909, when its surroundings were still semi-rural and poor. Contains paintings of Benedito Calixto and Oscar Pereira da Silva.

see.n: Our Lady of Good Death Church
see.b: Known in the past as “Igreja das Boas Notícias” (Church of Good News) due to its bells tolling whenever someone important arrived in São Paulo, the historical church opened in 1810. Local legend says its curious name is due to the fact…
A church from the colonial period, finished in 1758, with the original building dating back to 1592. Contains over a hundred pieces of art from the colonial area.

Built in a neo-romantic style with neo-gothic details, it resembles medieval churches in northern Europe. It was temporarily the cathedral of São Paulo between 1930 and 1954. Contains paintings of Henri Bernard, Benedito Calixto and…
Former São Paulo city hall, constructed during the 1920s in an eclectic style. It now hosts an interactive science museum, a very popular choice to take the kids to.
Focused on showcasing Latin American artists, with the entrance changing its painting whenever there's a new exhibition. Ironically, despite being named "Red Gallery", the walls are mostly white.

Dedicated to those who fought against the military dictatorship in Brazil, which occurred from 1964 to 1985. Here you can see prison cells, written documents, spoken testimonies and visual records of this period.

Dedicated to one of the city's founders, José de Anchieta, and also the place where São Paulo was founded on January 25, 1554. It contains many paintings and historic documents, the most interesting of which is a scale model of early…
Ran by Fundação Armando Alvares Penteado (FAAP), an arts university. Houses a variety of temporary exhibitions.
With its wealth of religious images (Natividade Musem is housed there), it is where Carmelite Nuns prepared Frei Galvão pills, which many consider to be miraculous.
Focused on the history of different kinds of energy that powered both São Paulo and the world, includes interactive exhibitions.

see.pr: R$25, free on Thursdays and Sundays
see.b: A interactive linguistics museum that shows the different accents and dialects of Portuguese in Europe, Africa, Asia and South America, as well as its relation to other tongues and their developments and influence of African,…

see.pr: R$42,50, free on Saturdays and the second Sunday of every month
see.b: High quality temporary exhibits share the stage with the museum’s fantastic painting and sculpture collection. Come early to avoid the crowds.

Since the early 20th century, this necropolis has buried some of the most well known figures in Brazil, such as Tarsila do Amaral, Mário de Andrade and Monteiro Lobato, many of them with beautiful sculptures carved for their graves. The…
One of the few green areas in the Center, it contains bronze statues by France artists, some built into fountains.

see.pr: R$ 24 for the museum, free for the stadium itself
see.b: One of the country's most important and iconic stadiums, Estádio do Pacaembu is an art deco giant built in 1940, and 10 years later hosted six matches of the 1950 FIFA World Cup. Since then, it has hosted several final matches for…

The other traditional address for classical music fans. The São Paulo State Symphony Orchestra (OSESP), an important symphony orchestra which represents the state, plays its concerts there. It’s also possible to pre-arrange guided…

Opened in 1929, this building's purpose changed along with its leadership, going from a movie theater to a live performance theater. Hosts the most popular Broadway-style musicals south of the equator, translated into Portuguese.

see.pr: Free to visit, price varies by presentation
see.b: One of the two traditional addresses for classical music fans. This is where the historic Modern Art Week took place in 1922. The building, designed by Ramos de Azevedo in 1911, is reason enough to justify a visit. It now houses the São…

The largest library in the city and the second largest in the country, named after the modernist artist. With over 3,2 million titles, it distinguishes itself for its collection of 60 thousand rare documents dating back to the 19th century.
Once the bank’s first headquarters in São Paulo — offers an excellent program of arts, movies, theater and music at accessible prices.
A general culture center where limited time events often take place. It has a library, movie theater and concerts. It is a common place for informal street dance and board game gatherings.

This cultural center of the Japanese diaspora contains the Japanese Immigration Museum, where visitors can learn about the history of the Japanese community in Brazil. A lot of activities are available, including Japanese courses and…

The historical part of downtown is known for being unsafe at night, so to compensate for that, local NGOs organize a nocturnal walking tour every Thursday. It is an opportunity to have a different look at some of downtown's most famous…
The largest festival of the Chinese community in São Paulo celebrates the Chinese new year. Celebrated every year with typical Chinese performances and food.

This traditional event of the Japanese community is celebrated every year around July. In this event, people write their wishes into pieces of paper and hang them into bamboo sticks. There is also a cosplay contest, typical Japanese…

see.a: R. 13 de Maio and R. Doutor Luiz Barreto
see.b: The largest festival of the Italian community in São Paulo, and also a religious event. Celebrated every year, it typically lasts the whole month. Includes typical Italian food, music and performances.

One of the oldest churches of São Paulo, its beautiful architecure stands out when it's lit up at night. Sitting at the top of a hill where a colonial-era village once stood, the statue of Our Lady of Penha from that time is still up.

The huge park, with 14 million square meters, is part of the larger Parque Várzeas do Tietê, which when finished, will cover most of the east part of the Tietê river. The visitable area is the south shore of the river, which includes…

Parque do Carmo has 9 million m², with the area open for visits having 1.5 million m² - the same size of Parque do Ibirapuera (see São Paulo/South Central). This causes the two parks to be often compared to each other, but they are…

see.a: Praça Padre Aleixo Monteiro Mafra, 11 - São Miguel Paulista
see.b: In the extreme east of São Paulo lies the oldest church of the city, constructed by native Brazilians in 1622. São Miguel was the name of the indigenous village, which would later become a neighborhood of São Paulo. The chapel…

see.a: Avenida Fernando Espírito Santo Alves de Mattos, 1000 - Parque do Carmo
see.b: Adjacent to Parque do Carmo, SESC Itaquera is one of the most important cultural, sport and recreation centers of the East. Highlights are the 5,000 square meters waterpark and the forest trails suited for families with kids. As other…

The largest and most well-known performance venue of the region. Musical presentations are usually from popular Brazilian music styles such as samba, pagode, forró, axé, sertanejo, and funk carioca (a style originary from Rio de…

see.h: Open only on Saturdays, Sundays and holidays from 16:00-23:00. They often extend the closing time a little more, but never beyond midnight.
see.b: The amusement park of Itaquera. Inaugurated in 1987 at its current location, the park has roller coaster, little train, electric cars, Viking ship, space ship, terror tunnel, and other fifteen rides. The tragic death of a passenger and…

Parque do Carmo is the place of São Paulo's most famous cherry blossom festival, a typical Japanese tradition. It happens annually around August. The festival is accompanied by Japanese food and cultural presentations, although the…

The charity bazaar, organized by a Japanese-founded association that takes care of mentally disabled people, is an atypical event, closely resembling a fair in the countryside of the state. It happens, in fact, in a weekend in July in…

While named an island, this is a peninsula, accessible from the city by ferry. Sitting within the Billings reservoir, this small area is mostly covered by nature and older houses, giving it a distinct small town profile compared to the…

A crater 400m deep and with 3.6 km diameter, created by the impact of a meteor between 1 and 20 million years ago. The crater now contains the Vargem Grande neighborhood, a humble 40,000-inhabitant area. The best view from the crater is…

Built in 1937 to connect the countryside of the state to its coast for cargo delivery, this long-decommissioned station is surrounded by a clump of mostly empty old houses and rivers crossing the area, giving its abandoned profile a…

see.a: Av. Dona Helena Pereira de Morais, 200
see.b: With 138,000 m², it is a relatively small but well-known park in the wealthy neighborhood of Panamby, containing a patch of Atlantic rainforest. In the center of the park lies a mansion built in the 19th century, which was briefly used…

An authentic Buddhist temple, constructed by Chinese immigrants in in the 1990's. They don't propose themselves as a tourist attraction, as such they can be stingy about accepting visitors, which require advance scheduling.

see.n: Sacred place of Church of the World Messianity
see.b: The Church of the World Messianity is a Japanese church that constructs their temples in special meditation areas, known as "Sacred places". It is open for visits for people from all religions. The Guarapiranga sacred place has 327,500…

If you want to know more about the life of native Brazilians without even leaving São Paulo, it is possible by means of a scheduled visit to one of these villages (called tekoa in the Guarani language). Activities include trails, music…
A small patch of woods, notable for its capybara and limpkin populations, the latter known for being noisy when communicating with the other birds who inhabit the location.
A flat park that's easy to have a walk on. Besides the pleasant scenery and plenty of open space, it has multiple sports venues to enjoy.
A larger park with exercise venues, boat rides, small farm lodges to sleep in and a trail that requires you to be blindfolded for a challenge.
Short trails, food stands, plenty of nature and views of the reservoir are available in this pleasant park.

see.n: Serra do Mar State Park - Curucutu Nucleus
see.b: Crossed by the rivers Capivari, Monos e Embu-Guaçu, this is a 25-million-m² park that constitutes the largest area of preserved Atlantic rainforest of the country. Aside from the extensive bodies of water that serve the city, the region…

A 2km, 1 hour-long, easy difficulty trail, taking you through the Embu-Guaçu river down to one of its sources. You are allowed to have a taste of the water at specific spots. Visits are self-guided, and up to 300 people can visit daily.

A 2km, 2h30min long, medium difficulty trail, taking you high into a great view of the city. Those lucky to get clear skies can see the state's coast and the Atlantic ocean in the distance. A guide is required, but can be arranged on…

eat.b: Korean street market with traditional food, K-pop dance contests and souvenirs available.

At this weekend open market, you can taste Asian delicacies like gyoza, takoyaki and okonomiyaki as well as non-Asian treats like acarajé from Bahia. Look for unusual sweets like ginger ice cream or even tempura-fried ice-cream.

A truly traditional outing in São Paulo, the "Big Market" is a mosaic of color and flavor that showcases a little something from all the different nationalities that settled in the capital. Pop in to sample the most beloved pastries and…
Burgers and sandwiches. Try the famous sanduíche de pernil, barbecued ham sandwich, the comfort food for many generations of journalists and students that roam around that region.
Hot dogs with unusual ingredients such as apple sauce, pork-based sandwiches and even ice cream with torresmo (deep-fried pork fat bits). Relaxed and young atmosphere.
Founded in 1922, this is the place where the famous bauru - a sandwich that comprises 4 types of cheese melted into a fondue, along with roast beef and tomato slices - was invented.
Fully vegan restaurant with an all-you-can-eat buffet at a fixed price during daytime. Offers a pizza buffet at night.

Typical Japanese ramen shop, where you are greeted with an irasshai-mase (welcome in Japanese) at the door and noodle-slurping noises from the Japanese customers. Also has great gyozas as side dishes.
Traditional Brazilian food with minor Japanese touches. Also serves yakisoba.
Italian cuisine in a rustic atmosphere. Live music on weekends.

A Chinese restaurant famous for authentic and tasty Cantonese dishes with cheap and generous portions. Communicating with the staff can be a challenge, as many only speak Chinese, but the food is worth the while. Reservations only for…
Japanese restaurant with an extensive menu. Try the fried oysters or the yosenabe, stewed white fish with vegetables.

If you are the kind of tourist who doesn't like to feel at all like a tourist, check this "factory-style" restaurant immensely popular among workers in the region, with long lines, self-service catering, and capacity for 400 people. The…
Traditional Italian restaurant in República, opened in 1951.

Chinese restaurant with a huge menu specializing in noodle dishes. At the right-hand corner of the main room, behind a glass window, the cook displays his ability to shape yakisoba noodles by hand. Seafood yakisoba is a good choice for…

Century-old barbecue restaurant that started as a bar. Plenty of cuts, sides and common paulistano dishes available. If you don't feel like it, they also have a burger shop and a cafe just crossing the street.
A bright, cheerful restaurant with a multi-cultural menu with items from a variety of countries from Peru to Italy to Thailand.
Restaurant and bar focused on pork dishes. Includes unique experiments such as raw pork temaki, along with a large drink selection and snacks to go.
Charming French bistro that is adorned with vintage posters and offers culinary delights such as homemade cherry strudels and roast lamb.
Very popular and traditional Italian restaurant. All dishes are made to serve two people. Buses of tourists come and go at the door. If going at peak time, expect a long wait to be seated.
Cozy French cuisine bistro with honest food and prices. Expect to find some of the classic dishes, such as steak tartare, steak poivre and moules et frites (mussels and chips).
One of the most traditional Italian cantinas in São Paulo. Try the polpetone, a kind of flat meatloaf filled with melted mozzarella cheese, for which special recipe this restaurant became famous for.
Renowned chef Marcos Bassi's "temple of meat" is one of the city's most famous steakhouses.
High-end Italian cuisine with a 360º view of the city.

One of the best places in São Paulo for live music, especially on Thursday and Sunday, when traditional samba plays. This bar was opened in the 1920s and is the most traditional place to hear classics of Brazilian Popular Music (MPB).
Opened in 1940. Go for the beer, served with a minimum of three fingers of foam. Always full and popular with locals and visitors alike.
The place to go for live music, especially jazz and blues. Has an old world feel with marble bar tops and antique balconies, but it's the perfect place to hear good music.
Small but pleasant LGBT-focused bar. Live music on some nights.
Electronic club at the center of São Paulo's nightlife street.
A mix of restaurant, karaoke and snooker bar, this unimaginable place packs on Thursdays and Fridays and is often featured on TV. Get in after 22:00.
70 year old Paulistano pizzeria, with lighter dough used.
Restaurant that serves traditional São Paulo food, with some of its ingredients coming straight from their farm. Try their juices, made with local fruit.
Enjoy live music and DJs on weekends. The bar/restaurant also has outside seating and a square on the same street.

eat.a: R. Antônio Hélio de Azevedo Marques, 72
eat.b: A reggae club with a somewhat long drink menu and a chill atmosphere.
A long-standing bakery in the region, with the expected bread and baked goods made to a high standard. They also take large orders for events, if made in advance.
Alongside bakery goods, they have a soup buffet and happy hour deals.
Provides a solid breakfast, with a variety of dishes from simple bread and butter on the grill (pão na chapa) to beirute (Lebanese-Brazilian steak sandwich).
Solid bakery that also serves rotisserie chicken to go on Sundays.
Active since 1984, this bakery became ingrained in the daily life of those living nearby. Solid treats and pizza even late at night.

This bakery is famed for its 1kg coxinha, allowing costumers to take on a challenge where it becomes free of charge if you eat it under 10 minutes. Normal-sized coxinhas are also available, and they are some of the very best in the city.

Brazilian panquecas (pancakes) are eaten more like crepes on a plate, rolled into a tube shape with savory or sweet fillings inside, topped with sauce. This restaurant offers solid pancakes alongside pasta and grilled dishes.

eat.a: R. Albertina Viêira da Silva Gordo, 326
eat.b: Nice selection of meat skewers, alongside tasty sandwiches. A convenience store is right across the street for cheap drinks.

Europeans might know the dish as döner kebab due to its Turkish diaspora, but São Paulo was more influenced by Syrian and Lebanese immigration, thus meat cuts with vegetables on a flat bread is known as shawarma. This establishment…
A long-running sit-down pizzeria, with a large menu of toppings, including vegan options.
Tex-Mex restaurant with a Brazilian touch, focused on appetizers and sharing plates, alongside an extensive drink menu. The fajitas (grilled meat and vegetables) are especially popular.

Very small sushi service, with some gimmicky options like hamburger and hot dog shaped hot rolls (breaded, deep-fried sushi). The standout is their poke, a large bowl of rice and fresh ingredients such as raw fish and vegetables.

While the menu signed by chef Rodrigo Oliveira and the Michelin Bib Gourmand award may make you think of this as a high-end fancy pants establishment, the atmosphere is casual and the dishes are very straightforward Northeastern…
Delivery-only fried chicken spot, serving large boxes with baked potatoes and dipping sauces as sides. A great option to eat in a group.
Hole-in-the-wall sushi shop specializing in temaki (sushi cones). The breaded spicy shrimp temaki is one of the standout fillings.
Countryside-themed buffet with many options of caipira food from São Paulo and Minas Gerais' farms.
Good pizza in a nicely decorated restaurant, with tasty appetizers and a wine list.
Straightforward Japanese rodízio (all you can eat), with an authorial drink menu.
Enjoy a drink while watching soccer, with straightforward bar snacks available. Coming on match day is recommended if you wanna mingle with the locals.

Active since 1970, this establishment became a favorite among locals for its snacks, drinks and easygoing atmosphere. Aside from their self-brewed beer and non-alcoholic drink menu, their bolinho fried snacks are well worth a try.
Formerly an Irish pub, now it's a very illumined dance club playing mainly retro music.
Brick walls enclose the cozy ambiance and pleasant drinks. The meals are expensive but easily feed two people.
Electronic music club, with birthday reservations available with drinks included.
Concert hall focused on small local artists, with drinks available on site.

eat.a: Largo Matriz de Nossa Senhora do Ó, 87, Freguesia do Ó
eat.b: Pizzeria founded in 1939, considered one of the best of the city.

eat.a: Largo da Matriz de Nossa Senhora do Ó, 168, Freguesia do Ó
eat.b: Place famous for its delicious coxinha, a popular Brazilian snack based on chicken, and for its large selection of international beers.
Many different cuisines are represented in this street market, with unique and trendy street food from all over the world.
Bakery that is popular with late night and early day locals, offers a high variety of breads, sweets and a sit down restaurant with options from breakfast all the way to dinner.
A quick bite of savory or sweet slices, with unique flavors such as shimeji available.
Small and cozy French restaurant by chef Erick Jacquin, popular in Brazil for multiple food-based reality TV shows.
A long standing address, known for its beirute, a Middle East dish adapted for the Brazilian palate. It uses flat bread, steak, vegetables and cheeses.

Finish your museum visit here, where you can taste a unique mix of food from Bahia and Minas Gerais with international fine dining influence. The baião de dois with beef stew is a popular option, and can be finished by a banana crème…
Modern Brazilian cuisine, with weekday deals for multi-course meals. The caipira lasagna is a stand-out vegetarian dish.
Stylishly modern in both decor and its fine dining dishes, with a focus on beef and pasta.
High-end sushi spot, serves fresh oysters.
Japanese-inspired coffee shop, with trendy ingredients such as matcha. Also has Japanese-inspired snacks.
Always full on weekends, this old school bar has a privileged view of the movement of the avenue.
Cheap and fresh fruit juice, many options available.
German-style beer served in large glasses, also has good snacks.
Sells many different empadas (mini pies with crumbly dough), alongside other snacks. Larger pies can be bought, but some have to be requested in advance.
A pastel (fried turnovers) shop that's been in service since 1967. Its pastéis are full of filling and crunchy.
Hamburger shop founded in 1969. Offers different kinds of sandwiches and has set itself as a traditional delivery service. Also offers milkshakes and a buffet.
Authentic Indian restaurant focused on lamb, chicken and vegetarian options.

Heavily themed fantasy restaurant, with creative dishes (try the onions with pork) and unique "potion" drinks. Also offers activities such as bow shooting. Reservations are always required, with 15+ person groups requiring a reservation…
High-end pizza, closer to Italian than Brazilian-style. The garden decoration stands out, and there's an extensive drink menu.
Nice pizza and snack restaurant, rodízio (all you can eat) style. Offers unusual toppings such as cod, shrimp and shiitake.
